check_security_updates.description: Ask whether a project needs updating, and whether it is urgent. Give it the version you run and it says plainly whether that release is one drupal.org has marked insecure, whether the project has been abandoned, and what to move to. Being on a release marked insecure is the thing to act on, and no version number can tell you that by itself. Run it over your module list on a schedule to get a standing security check.

description: Work with Drupal from a workflow, in two halves. The first needs nothing at all: search drupal.org for any of its tens of thousands of modules, themes and distributions, read a project's releases, look through issue queues, and find contributors. The action worth having on a schedule is the security check, which takes the version you run and tells you whether drupal.org has marked it insecure, whether the project has been abandoned, and what to move to. The second half talks to a Drupal site of your own over JSON:API, which ships in core: list, read, create, change and delete content, taxonomy terms, users and anything else in its content model, with a raw request action for the rest. Add the site URL and an account to switch that half on; everything about drupal.org keeps working without one.
